mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing the permission matrix allows non-permitted roles to perform operations. The LeastPrivilege assertion validates that all operations respect the matrix; removing the matrix definition allows violations.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_UnauthorisedOperation { some op: AccessOperation, role: ClinicianRole | op.clinician.role = role and not (role -> op.operation in PermMatrix.Allowed) }

mutation_targets.rationale: This fact ensures audit entry fields match the operation that created them. Removing it allows misattributed audit entries, which violates both the completeness assertion (mismatched outcomes) and attribution correctness.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditMismatch { some op: AccessOperation, ae: AuditEntry | op.auditEntry = ae and op.clinician.id != ae.clinicianId }

mutation_targets.rationale: This fact enforces unique-audit-entry mappings per operation, preventing audit duplication or mutation. Removing it allows an operation to map to multiple distinct audit entries, violating the append-only invariant.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditDuplication { some disj ae1, ae2: AuditEntry, op: AccessOperation | op.auditEntry = ae1 and ae1 = ae2 }

mutation_targets.rationale: This fact encodes the access-control decision tree: permitted access requires active membership, denied/not-found outcomes follow from missing membership or non-existent patient. Removing it allows a clinician without care-team membership to access a patient record.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AccessBypassCareTeam { some op: AccessOperation, ctm: CareTeamMembership | op.operation = RecordsLookup and op.outcome = Permitted and not (ctm.clinician = op.clinician and ctm.patient.id = op.patientId and ctm.status = Active) }

mutation_targets.rationale: This fact ensures that denied and not-found outcomes are observationally equivalent (both return non-Permitted status). Removing it allows the system to leak information by distinguishing them.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_LeakageViaResponse { some op1, op2: AccessOperation | (op1.outcome = Denied or op1.outcome = NotFoundOrDenied) and op2.outcome = Permitted }

mutation_targets.rationale: This fact enforces that every operation respects the permission matrix. Removing it allows unpermitted (role, operation) pairs to execute.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_UnpermittedOp { some op: AccessOperation | not (op.clinician.role -> op.operation in PermMatrix.Allowed) }
